premises: Static and dynamic lattice distortions in HEAs can be unified via an effective temperature scaling law
Lattice thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr is nearly temperature-independent (~6 W/(K·m)) at 50–300 K
Electronic thermal conductivity increases roughly linearly with temperature in this alloy
Decoupling lattice and electronic contributions yields ~50% less predictive error than prior models
Wiedemann-Franz law can be used to separate electronic from lattice conductivity
